title: Complex presentation and canonical maps of uniformly bounded below derived hypersheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ of covering sieves, let $s$ contain its object and morphism universes [def-weil-size-convention], let $R$ be a commutative ring in $\mathrm{Type}_s$, and let $a\in\mathbb Z$. Use set-valued sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. A semirepresentable presheaf is a presheaf isomorphic to the coproduct of representables of an $s$-small formal family [def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct]. A semirepresentable hypercover is an augmented simplicial set presheaf $U_\bullet\to h_T$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] with semirepresentable levels and with every proper-face matching arrow in the presheaf slice over $h_T$ an epimorphism after sheafification. Proper-face matching means the canonical boundary limit arrow [lem-weil-pbc-site-hypercover-disjoint-union]; in degree zero its target is the terminal object of the slice. Neither subcanonicity nor fibre products in $\mathcal C$ are assumed.

Put $\mathcal P_R=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}_R)$. Linearize a hypercover sectionwise with the free $R$-module functor. Its alternating-face chain complex, extended to cochain degrees $0,-1,-2,\ldots$, has its actual augmentation $\epsilon_U:R[U_\bullet]\to R[h_T][0]$. A complex $M$ of $\mathcal P_R$ has hyperdescent when precomposition with $\epsilon_U$ is a quasi-isomorphism on full global product Hom complexes for every such hypercover. Use the full Hom differential and canonical pre/postcomposition maps [lem-coef-sheaf-flat-model]. The free terms are sums of projective representables, so these Hom complexes are the derived hypercover totalizations, with products on families, in the enhanced derived sense [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The pointwise bound $M\ge a$ means $H^i(M(T))=0$ for every $T\in\mathcal C$ and $i<a$. Let $\mathrm{Rep}_{J,R,\ge a}$ be the full category of complexes satisfying hyperdescent and this bound, and let $W$ be its objectwise quasi-isomorphisms. A presentation of $\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}(\mathcal C,R)$ is a quasicategory $\mathcal H$ and a map $q:N(\mathrm{Rep}_{J,R,\ge a})\to\mathcal H$ satisfying the entire coherent-functor-category localization universal property for $W$ [lem-coef-sheaf-flat-model, def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. This is presentation data, not a choice from an unproved existence assertion.

For a functor $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, strict restriction is termwise precomposition by $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ and strict right Kan extension is the ordinary presheaf right Kan functor applied termwise. The latter is additive as a right adjoint. Its counit is the presheaf Kan counit termwise. At $D$, the actual comma cone has apex $(\operatorname{Ran}_{p^{\mathrm{op}}}I)(D)$, index $\operatorname{StructuredArrow}(D,p^{\mathrm{op}})\cong(p\downarrow D)^{\mathrm{op}}$, and legs induced by restriction followed by the counit. Enlarging by the canonical $\operatorname{AsSmall}$ equivalences only aligns universes. A coefficient presentation is the analogous coherent quasi-isomorphism localization of all $R$-module complexes. The comma cone is a derived limit when its actual localized apex and its entire localized coherent transformation give a terminal object in the coherent cone category [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Restriction and right Kan functors on the full representative subcategories are defined whenever their hyperdescent and bound-preservation proofs are supplied; right Kan uses K-injective representatives. The canonical full Hom-complex restriction map is induced degreewise by the additive restriction functor. All these constructions retain their actual differentials, maps and coherent localization data.
